# Avia playbook (`search_avia` -> `create_checkout_link`)

## Detail card
No confirmed read-only avia detail endpoint. For a presentation card,
pass the selected compact offer object as `details_ref` to
`get_offer_details(product_type='avia', ...)` — it reformats with no
side effects.

## Flight number
The flight number is `legs[].segments[].voyage_no` (e.g. `SU-6026`) — one
per segment, so a connection shows one number per hop. Quote it verbatim;
never reconstruct a flight number from the carrier name or times.

## Filters (`direct_only`, `carriers`)
`direct_only=true` keeps only nonstop flights (every leg a single segment;
round-trip stays direct when both legs are). `carriers=[...]` keeps only offers
where every listed airline matches one of the requested names/ids; a mixed
Aeroflot+S7 offer does not satisfy "only Aeroflot".
`meta.carriers_available` is the per-route airline reference DERIVED from the
fetched offers (avia fetches the full route pool, so it's complete for the
route): each entry has `name` ("Аэрофлот"), `offers_count` and `price_from` —
plus a stable `id` ("1062") ONLY when Tutu ships its carrier facet (the current
`/avia/offers` endpoint doesn't — see the TODO-for-Tutu; filter by `name`).
Matching is a case-insensitive substring on the name, so guessing ("aeroflot"
for "Аэрофлот") silently drops everything. What
each filter removed is in `meta.post_filter_dropped_not_direct` /
`post_filter_dropped_wrong_carrier`. When a filter is active the whole route
pool is fetched before filtering, so an airline listed in `carriers_available`
reliably shows up in the filtered result and `has_more` stays honest — no thin
page from the page-scoped fetch. `meta.total_matched` is the exact count after
filters (before pagination): "сколько всего рейсов Азимута" is one search, not a
page-walk (`meta.total_matched_exact=false` only on a rare >200-offer route).

## Exact flight — «возьми рейс N»
A results page is a window over the matched flights, NOT the day's
timetable — a flight absent from the current page may still operate, so
never conclude «рейса N нет» from one page while `meta.has_more` is true.
When the user names a flight, pass `flight_numbers=['SU-6176']` — any
spelling of the designator works ('SU 6176', 'su6176', leading zeros),
and bare digits ('6176') match by flight number alone;
`meta.post_filter_dropped_wrong_flight_number` counts the rest. A
connection or round-trip containing the flight is kept WHOLE. An empty
NUMBER-ONLY result means «этого рейса нет в продаже на Tutu на эту
дату» — the flight may still operate (sold out or not sold here); say
that, never a timetable claim. That reading holds only while
`meta.total_matched_exact` is true: on a rare capped route (`false`)
the filter saw a truncated pool, so the check is INCONCLUSIVE — and no
in-tool filter can rescue it (`carriers` / `price_max` cut the SAME
truncated prefix, they never widen the pool). Hand the user the
`search_results_url` (the full listing on tutu.ru) instead of
concluding «нет».
And with other filters also active (`price_max` / `carriers` /
`direct_only` / airport scope) even «нет в продаже» doesn't follow —
the flight may be dropped by one of those (each counts its removals in
`meta.post_filter_dropped_*`); re-run number-only before concluding.

## Airport-scoped search (input)
`origin` / `destination` accept a specific airport as well as a city — by
name («Шереметьево», «Внуково») or bare IATA code («SVO», «IST»). Tutu's
search runs city-wide, so the server narrows the result to the requested
airport itself: offers via other airports of the same city are dropped and
counted in `meta.post_filter_dropped_wrong_airport` (the key is present
only when the request named a specific airport). The narrowed
endpoint carries
`meta.from/to.kind="airport"` and its `iata` is the AIRPORT's code (for a
city input `iata` is the city code, e.g. MOW). On a round-trip both legs
are held to the airport (out arrives there, return departs there). If
every city flight uses other airports, `meta.airport_note` lists them with
counts — relay it and offer to re-search by city name. A bare IATA code
means the airport, not the metro area: «IST» is Стамбул-Новый only (SAW
dropped), while «Стамбул» covers all airports. Pass the city name whenever
the user doesn't care about the airport.

## Place resolution (`meta.from` / `meta.to`)
Each side echoes the place that was searched: `name`, `geo_id`, `region`.
`match` + `query` are present only when the resolved name differs from
the wording you sent — `lead` (Tutu's own ranking read a short form or
typo: «Питер», «Масква»), `qualified` (the trailing words acted as a
region filter: «Красная Поляна, Краснодарский край»), `prefix` (the name
was completed). Say which place came back and keep going; a synonym is
never a reason to stop and confirm. `also_named[]` lists same-name places
that lost to a better-connected one — mention them with a one-line
invitation to correct, never as a blocking question.
Two wordings are refused with an error instead of being searched as some
other city, and the error text is the instruction:
- `could not resolve … N places share this name and none is better
  connected …` — an exact-name tie. The candidates are listed with their
  regions, and the text may add what Tutu's hotel index lists under this
  name. Ask the user which one is meant, or resend as '<name>, <область
  или район>' (name first, no parentheses). Do not pick one yourself.
- `could not resolve … no place with this name in Tutu's transport index
  …` — the fuzzy suggestions were unrelated places and were NOT searched.
  If the text says Tutu's hotel index lists it, hotels there ARE
  searchable — say so and offer `search_hotels`; never report it as
  «транспорта нет». Otherwise check the spelling with the user.
`… has no <id> in Tutu's index` means the place resolved but this
transport has no node there — ask for a place that has one; when the text
names the city Tutu's avia index answered with, offer it and search it
only after the user agrees. `Tutu's geo index did not answer` is a
transient upstream error: retry the call.

Avia adds one refusal of its own: a place without an airport (`avia
cannot search … has no avia_id in Tutu's index`). The text names the city
Tutu's avia index answered with for that wording (e.g. Сочи for Хоста) —
offer that city to the user and search it only after they agree; never
search it on your own, and never guess an airport city silently.

## Checkout
`create_checkout_link` (transport=avia) returns BOTH:
- `checkout_url` — a Tutu `mtp-deeplink/explicit/avia` that leads STRAIGHT
  to the cart for this exact ticket: it mints the cart and 302s to
  `checkout.tutu.ru/cart/<id>` (sometimes via a short loader page). There
  is no seat picker in front of it — unlike rail/bus/hotels, whose default
  link is a selection page. Falls back to the search results if the offer
  is no longer available.
- `search_results_url` — the listing page for browsing.
Round-trip: a direct round-trip offer (`checkout_ref.is_round_trip=true`,
one flight outbound + one flight return) now returns a real two-leg deeplink —
it mints a cart with BOTH the outbound and return legs. Forward
`is_round_trip` AND `return_departure_at` from `checkout_ref`; without
`return_departure_at` the tool can't encode the return leg and falls back to
the search page (`kind="search_redirect"`). Connecting round-trips (3+ flights
total, at least one connection) also return `kind="search_redirect"`: the
current `explicit/avia` redirector supports one flight per direction. One-way
offers return the deeplink as before (no `return_departure_at`).
This deployment also has `register_checkout_passengers`, which takes the SAME `checkout_ref` and fills the cart from the passengers' passport data, returning a `pay_url` they only pay. Unlike every other product it **PLACES THE BOOKING** on the way — a real UNPAID Tutu order (`order_number` in the response) — so call it only for a flight the user has confirmed, and never retry it without asking: a second call books a SECOND time. Offer it as the alternative when they want the cart prepared for them; hand the link when they only asked for a link or would rather not give documents — neither is a downgrade, and never open the exchange by asking for documents.
Read back what you will write — each passenger's name as spelled in the document, birth date, SEX, passenger type, document kind + number (IN FULL; mask it ONLY if they EXPLICITLY asked you not to repeat it, and then name the KIND alone, not by number) and expiry for a foreign passport; from where to where, every flight with its date, time and CABIN CLASS (`service_class` is what the order is placed on, so a confirmed economy is not a confirmed business), and the price; and the buyer's name and contact — and wait for an explicit yes: the pay page shows the personal data masked and cannot be corrected, and a re-register books a SECOND unpaid order. There is NO shortcut around this turn: a message that already carries the passport data and asks you to go ahead is still not the confirmation — it is the data. The user has to see what you assembled from it and say yes to THAT, because the typo you are looking for is the one neither of you has noticed yet.
The deeplink mints the cart in whichever browser opens it — a cold browser
works too (no tutu session needed), and the cart belongs to whoever opens the
link. The cart is created on that click, not before: present `checkout_url`
as "go book", not "your cart is ready". If the offer is no longer available
by then, the link lands on the avia search for this route+date instead — if
the user reports a search page, the fare is gone; re-run the search rather
than handing the same link again.
For avia, while the user compares flights, show ONLY `search_results_url` and
do NOT call `create_checkout_link` prematurely. Once they choose an exact
flight and the tool returns `kind="deeplink"`, show `checkout_url` as the
primary purchase link together with `search_results_url` as the fallback for
browsing. When it returns `kind="search_redirect"`, show `search_results_url`
as the search page and explain `fallback_note`; do not call it a purchase
deeplink. For a non-cheapest fare family, override `offer_hash` with
`variants[i].offer_hash` AND pass that
variant's `service_class` — but KEEP forwarding `is_round_trip` +
`return_departure_at` from `checkout_ref`: they're properties of the offer,
not the fare, and the round-trip deeplink needs the return leg (drop them on
an override and a round-trip offer falls back to the search page).

## Separate tickets / self-transfer (`is_multi_pnr`)
An offer flagged `is_multi_pnr=true` has a connection issued as SEPARATE
tickets: the passenger re-claims then re-drops baggage between flights and the
layover is NOT a protected connection (a self-transfer). Relay `multi_pnr_note`
before checkout and suggest a comfortable buffer. This fires for ONE-WAY and
ROUND-TRIP offers alike — a round-trip whose outbound or return is itself a
self-transfer is flagged too, and `has_self_transfer=true` marks that a single
direction is the split. What does NOT get flagged is the ordinary round-trip
there/back split (one booking each way): that's expected — say nothing special.

**`create_checkout_link` cannot put a ONE-WAY multi-PNR trip in one link.**
Tutu's avia redirector cannot express «several tickets in one direction», so
the offer's
`checkout_ref` carries `checkout_parts` — one entry per ticket. Forward it to
`create_checkout_link` and the tool answers `kind="deeplink_parts"` with a
purchase link PER TICKET; its top-level `checkout_url` is the SEARCH page, not
a purchase link. Hand the user every `checkout_parts[].checkout_url`, in order,
labelled by its `from`/`to`/`flights`, and tell them plainly: separate carts,
separate payments, buying only the first strands them at the connection. The
quoted price is the TOTAL for all tickets — the per-ticket split appears only
in each cart — and prices/seats can move between the two purchases. Omit
`checkout_parts` and the tool can only return the search page.

That limit is the LINK path's, not the trip's: this deployment also has `register_checkout_passengers`, which takes the SAME `checkout_ref` and mints ONE cart for the whole itinerary — one payment, one `pay_url`. It needs the user's passport data and it PLACES THE BOOKING, so offer it as the alternative when they want the trip prepared for them; hand the per-ticket links when they only asked for a link or would rather not give documents. Never present either as the only possibility. Read back what you will write — each passenger's name as spelled in the document, birth date, SEX, passenger type, document kind + number (IN FULL; mask it ONLY if they EXPLICITLY asked you not to repeat it, and then name the KIND alone, not by number) and expiry for a foreign passport; from where to where, EVERY flight of the itinerary with its date, time and CABIN CLASS (`service_class` is what the order is placed on, so a confirmed economy is not a confirmed business), and the price; and the buyer's name and contact — and wait for an explicit yes: the pay page shows the personal data masked and cannot be corrected, and a re-register books a SECOND unpaid order. There is NO shortcut around this turn: a message that already carries the passport data and asks you to go ahead is still not the confirmation — it is the data. The user has to see what you assembled from it and say yes to THAT, because the typo you are looking for is the one neither of you has noticed yet.

Pass the searched party — `passengers_full` (adults), `passengers_child`,
`passengers_infant` — from `checkout_ref` into `create_checkout_link`. The
deeplink requests exactly those passengers; omit them and Tutu defaults the
cart to ONE adult, so a 2-adult / family total you quoted won't match what
the user sees. Have the user confirm the passenger count in the cart
before paying. The full input
field list is in `create_checkout_link`'s own description.

## Airport disambiguation (mandatory)
Many cities have several airports: Стамбул IST / SAW, Москва SVO / DME /
VKO / ZIA, London LHR / LGW / STN / LTN, Paris CDG / ORY / BVA.
- Read the airport from `legs[].segments[].to` — a self-describing string
  `"City — Name (IATA), терм. T"` (e.g. `"Стамбул — Сабиха Гёкчен (SAW)"`,
  `"Москва — Внуково (VKO), терм. A"`). Surface it verbatim: the airport
  name and terminal come straight from the Tutu response, so prefer them
  over the bare code. When the upstream omitted the name the string falls
  back to `"City, IATA"` — then the IATA code is the signal; map it to a
  name only if you're sure (stable global registry, the ONE carve-out from
  the no-general-knowledge rule), otherwise show the code as-is.
- When two offers in one list use different airports of the same city,
  call it out explicitly using the airport names and IATA codes returned by
  the current MCP response. Say that they are different airports; do not add
  distance, side-of-city or transfer facts unless the payload returned them.
- Don't assume the user prefers the primary airport; surface both, never
  silently drop the secondary.

## Cashback
Flights earn none today, so `meta.cashback` is normally absent — say
nothing about cashback on an avia answer. If the key IS there (Tutu runs
campaigns), it is the whole page's Tutu loyalty rate: bonus points credited
to the buyer's Tutu account after payment, NOT money off `price`. Never
present it as a discount or net it off the fare. `applies_to` is
`all_fares` / `most_fares` / `some_fares`, with `rows_at_rate` of
`rows_total` fare rows on the last two; `exceptions[]` names the rows on a
different rate and may be capped.

## Grounding
Baggage, cabin baggage, refund/change rules, fare-family name, seat policy
and carrier rating must trace to `variants[].conditions` or
`review_summary` in the response. If a field is null/absent, say so —
never fall back to general carrier knowledge or web search.

# Hotels playbook (`search_hotels` -> `get_offer_details` ->
`create_checkout_link`)

## Checkout
Hotels have an `explicit/hotel` deeplink,
the same stateless handoff family as the transport tools — the user opens
the link and Tutu builds the cart in THEIR browser session (cold browser
works). `create_checkout_link` (product_type=hotels) has TWO modes off the
row's `checkout_ref`:
- **Page (default, `kind="deeplink"`)** — `hotel_alias` + dates + guests
  (+ `search_id`) open the hotel page with everything pre-filled for the
  user to pick a room. This is the official replacement for the old
  `offers/details` page link.
- **Straight-to-cart (`kind="checkout_deeplink"`)** — also pass an
  `offer_pack_hash` and the link mints the cart for that pack. It MUST be a
  SPECIFIC room rate's `offerpack_hash` from `get_offer_details`
  (`rooms[].rates[].offerpack_hash`). The listing `best_offer.offerpack_hash`
  does NOT mint a cart — the redirector falls back
  to the hotel page — so it's not carried in `checkout_ref`; get the cart hash
  from a room the user actually picked (same shape as rail seats from
  `get_rail_seatmap`). A stale/unbookable pack lands on the hotel page instead
  of erroring (`fallback_to_details`), so this mode is always safe.
This deployment also has `register_checkout_passengers`, which takes a ROOM rate's `offerpack_hash` (`product_source="hotels"`) and fills the cart from the guests' data, returning a `pay_url` they only pay. It books NOTHING and charges nothing (unlike avia, which places a real unpaid order). Same hash rule as the link: a ROOM rate's, never the listing `best_offer.offerpack_hash`. The document here is a `SIMPLE_DOCUMENT`, not a passport. Offer it as the alternative when the guest wants the cart prepared for them; hand the link when they only asked for a link or would rather not give documents — neither is a downgrade, and never open the exchange by asking for documents.
Read back what you will write — each passenger's name as spelled in the document, birth date, SEX, passenger type, document kind + number (IN FULL; mask it ONLY if they EXPLICITLY asked you not to repeat it, and then name the KIND alone, not by number) and expiry for a foreign passport; the hotel and its city, the room and rate, the check-in / check-out dates and the price; and the buyer's name and contact — and wait for an explicit yes: the pay page shows the personal data masked and cannot be corrected, and a re-register mints ANOTHER cart. There is NO shortcut around this turn: a message that already carries the passport data and asks you to go ahead is still not the confirmation — it is the data. The user has to see what you assembled from it and say yes to THAT, because the typo you are looking for is the one neither of you has noticed yet.
`best_offer.checkout_url` (on every search row) is the direct-page
FALLBACK, not the primary hand-off — reach for it when the tool's link
isn't available. (If a ref lacks `hotel_alias`, the tool returns that
same page with `kind="hotel_page"`.)

## geo_id: hotels vs transport (critical)
`search_hotels` resolves `city_name` against Tutu's hotel-specific geo
index — the same one hotel.tutu.ru's search box uses — NOT the transport
suggest. It is region-aware: for a resort zone it picks the `region` that
aggregates the sibling посёлки (e.g. «Курорт "Архыз"» covers посёлок
Архыз + Романтик + Нижний Архыз; the Роза Хутор region covers a locality
that is near-empty on its own), and for a plain city it picks that city.
`meta.resolved_geo` tells you what it searched: `geo_type`
(`region` | `locality`), `hotels_count` (catalog size), and `also_geo`
(the narrower/alternative geos sharing the name).
- ALWAYS prefer `city_name`. State which `resolved_geo.name` was searched;
  when `geo_type=region`, you may add that it covers the whole resort
  zone, and offer an `also_geo` locality if the user wants to narrow.
- **A specific hotel you don't see on page 1 is NOT a different geo.** The
  list is relevance-sorted and a region holds hundreds of properties, so a
  named hotel (especially a new / 0-review one) is usually just deeper —
  paginate (`page`+`page_size`, `meta.has_more`) or fetch it directly with
  `get_offer_details` by its `hotel_id`. Do NOT tell the user it lives in a
  separate geo_id; the region search already spans the zone.
- If you must pass `geo_id`, take it ONLY from a previous `search_hotels`
  response (`meta.geo_id` / `meta.resolved_geo.geo_id` / `also_geo[].geo_id`).
  NEVER reuse a `geo_id` / `from_geo_id` / `to_geo_id` from `search_avia` /
  `search_rail` / `search_bus` / `search_etrain` / `search_multitransport`
  — those are transport entries (airports, stations) and frequently have no
  hotels. Symptom: empty `hotels[]` with `meta.total_returned=0` while
  transport search worked.

## Clarifying questions
When a hotel search has many viable options and the user's message does
NOT pin the narrowing preferences (bed setup, breakfast, free
cancellation, view), do NOT call `search_hotels` yet — ask ONE short batch
(2-4 questions) FIRST, then search. This is a pre-call gate, not a
final-answer step: the mistake is starting the search before knowing what
to narrow by.
- Ask once, concise: bed setup (one double vs two singles), breakfast
  included, free cancellation, view / floor / balcony. With children ->
  also extra bed / cot and family-friendly amenities. Don't re-ask things
  already in the message (dates, city, guest count).
- **The gate is off the moment the user hands you the decision.** A
  deterministic selection rule ("первый найденный", "самый дешёвый",
  "выбери сам", "любой", "лишь бы переночевать", "без уточняющих
  вопросов") or an explicit checkout intent ("оформляй", "кинь ссылку")
  means the preferences you were NOT told are the ones the user doesn't
  care about. Don't ask — search, apply their rule to the actual results,
  and hand over the link in the SAME turn. Treat this as a closed list of
  wordings at your peril: judge the intent, not the phrase. Ask only for a
  REQUIRED field you genuinely cannot fill (city, dates) — a preference is
  never that field.
- Generic positive framing ("хорошее место", "бюджет не критичен") is NOT
  a selection rule and pins nothing — ask anyway.
- Map answers to filters: view/balcony/AC -> `room_amenities`; breakfast
  -> `breakfast_included=true`; free cancel -> `free_cancellation=true`;
  kid-friendly -> `hotel_amenities=['kid_friendly']`; property type
  (санаторий, глэмпинг, хостел, апартаменты…) -> `hotel_types`; bed
  preference -> annotate from `rooms[].bed_type` in `get_offer_details`
  (no listing-level bed filter today).
- The looser alternatives Tutu pads a filtered page with are dropped, so an
  empty `hotels[]` under filters means Tutu has no match («на эти даты
  санаториев нет») — say so and offer to drop a filter.

## One card = one row = one room
`get_offer_details` takes the hotel id as `offer_id`, `hotel_id` or
`hotel_geo_id` — three names for the same value, so copy whichever the
search row shows and pass exactly ONE. Passing two different ids is an
error, not a preference: it means two rows got mixed.
Each detail response echoes what it is about — `hotel.hotel_id`,
`hotel.name`, `hotel.alias` and `stay {check_in, check_out, nights,
guests}`. Check that echo against the row you meant before you write the
card, especially after a failed call: a rejected call is a reason to fix
the argument NAME, never to try a neighbouring id.
When you present several candidates, build each card from ONE room object
of ONE detail response — `room_name`, `room_size_sqm`, `view`,
`price_from` and the link all come off that object. Never carry a field
sideways from another room or hotel: two rooms of the same hotel routinely
differ only by a word and a metre («Полулюкс, терраса» 39 м² vs «Люкс,
терраса, вид на море» 40 м²), and a card assembled from both describes an
offer that doesn't exist.

## best_offer vs get_offer_details
`best_offer` describes ONLY the cheapest visible rate of one room. For room
categories (standard / comfort / suite), beds, view, size and full
per-rate options, call `get_offer_details`. Each room carries `price_from`
— its OWN cheapest rate, in the same `{amount, currency, price_basis}`
shape as a rate price. Quote that instead of scanning `rates[]` and
picking a minimum by hand; `rates[]` is for comparing meal / cancellation
/ payment options WITHIN the room you already chose. It defaults to
`view='compact'`:
photos are capped, the per-rate `cancellation_policy` ladder text is
omitted (the `free_cancellation` + `free_cancellation_until` flags stay,
so you can still state the policy in one line), room `amenity_groups`
are omitted (the flat `room_amenities` list stays), hotel
`amenity_groups` keep only group + amenity names, and review TEXTS are
omitted — the `review_summary` aggregate (rating, count, aspects) stays.
For the exact cancellation ladder ask `view='rules'`; for guest quotes
(плюсы/минусы from real reviews) ask `view='reviews'` + `review_limit` —
it returns `hotel.reviews[]` with `texts[].sentiment` (pros/cons) and
pagination; `view='full'` returns everything.

## Pricing — whole-stay totals
Every hotel price the tools return is the TOTAL for the requested stay and
guest composition, with the nights already multiplied in: the listing
`best_offer.price`, each `get_offer_details` `rooms[].rates[].price` — both
tagged `price_basis="stay_total"`. Render the number as returned and NEVER
multiply it by the night count; doing so double-counts and overstates the
price. `stay.nights` (top-level in both responses) is only for labelling,
e.g. "42 000 ₽ за 2 ночи". `price_max` is a PER-NIGHT budget — the server
enforces it as `price / stay.nights`, so pass the nightly figure.

## Grounding for asked-for features
Surface the raw field value next to each recommendation and judge
match-vs-mismatch with plain judgment (no decision table).
- View, bed setup -> room-level: `rooms[i].view`, `rooms[i].bed_type`.
- Room area -> in m². The LISTING `best_offer.room_size_sqm` is the more
  reliable source (parsed from the search room_name, e.g. «… от 16 кв.м»);
  `rooms[i].room_size_sqm` in details is usually `null` (Tutu's detail
  upstream rarely carries area). Often a MINIMUM (Tutu's «от N») — label
  «от N м²», don't read it as exact. `null` means Tutu didn't write a size
  (the common case) — say «Tutu не указал площадь», never assume it fails
  or passes a «>35 м²» ask. Do NOT silently drop hotels with unknown size:
  surface the value (or its absence) and let the user decide — a hard size
  cut would empty the list exactly where data is thin (e.g. Сен-Тропе: no
  hotel exposes a size, so a «>35 м²» filter would return zero).
- Breakfast, free cancellation, pay-at-hotel -> RATE-level (rates of one
  room can disagree): `rooms[i].rates[j].*`; in the listing the cheapest
  rate mirrors to `best_offer.breakfast_included` /
  `best_offer.free_cancellation`.
- `view` enum (source `app/repository/hotel_badges.py`): `sea` (explicit
  «на море/океан»), `water` (generic «на воду» — may be pond/canal, NOT

# Etrain playbook — commuter / suburban trains (электрички)
(`search_etrain` -> `create_checkout_link`)

## Station disambiguation (mandatory)
A city often has several commuter stations far apart — СПб (Московский /
Ладожский / Балтийский …), Москва (the radial вокзалы). The departure /
arrival point is in `legs[].segments[].from|to` as a self-describing
string `"City — Station (code)"` (e.g. `"Санкт-Петербург — Московский
вокзал (2004003)"`). Always name the concrete station when comparing
offers — never present two electrichkas that leave the same city from
different stations as if they share an origin, and never make the user
read the station out of the checkout URL.

## Place resolution (`meta.from` / `meta.to`)
Each side echoes the place that was searched: `name`, `geo_id`, `region`.
`match` + `query` are present only when the resolved name differs from
the wording you sent — `lead` (Tutu's own ranking read a short form or
typo: «Питер», «Масква»), `qualified` (the trailing words acted as a
region filter: «Красная Поляна, Краснодарский край»), `prefix` (the name
was completed). Say which place came back and keep going; a synonym is
never a reason to stop and confirm. `also_named[]` lists same-name places
that lost to a better-connected one — mention them with a one-line
invitation to correct, never as a blocking question.
Two wordings are refused with an error instead of being searched as some
other city, and the error text is the instruction:
- `could not resolve … N places share this name and none is better
  connected …` — an exact-name tie. The candidates are listed with their
  regions, and the text may add what Tutu's hotel index lists under this
  name. Ask the user which one is meant, or resend as '<name>, <область
  или район>' (name first, no parentheses). Do not pick one yourself.
- `could not resolve … no place with this name in Tutu's transport index
  …` — the fuzzy suggestions were unrelated places and were NOT searched.
  If the text says Tutu's hotel index lists it, hotels there ARE
  searchable — say so and offer `search_hotels`; never report it as
  «транспорта нет». Otherwise check the spelling with the user.
`… has no <id> in Tutu's index` means the place resolved but this
transport has no node there — ask for a place that has one; when the text
names the city Tutu's avia index answered with, offer it and search it
only after the user agrees. `Tutu's geo index did not answer` is a
transient upstream error: retry the call.

## Consist type and «билет с местом или просто сел и поехал?»
Each segment may carry `vehicle_meta` ({name, code, description,
seat_assignment}) — use it to filter consist type without parsing labels.

`seat_assignment` answers the seating question DIRECTLY and is the only
thing you may answer it from. Two values:

- `reserved` — the ticket names a seat. Tutu says so itself; `description`
  is the sentence it says it in.
- `unknown` — Tutu did NOT state it. Say that out loud: «Tutu не сообщает,
  закрепляется ли место». Then quote whatever it DID say from
  `description` (an «Экспресс» ticket, say) — that is information, just not
  the answer. Never turn `unknown` into «свободная рассадка»: those are
  different claims and only one of them is in the data.

`online_check_in` in the detail card's `ticket` block is a DIFFERENT
property and says nothing about seating — do not reason from it.

Two consist codes look alike and are not: `swallow` is «Ласточка (с
местом)» and `swallowBlue` is «Ласточка». The seat is exactly what
separates them, so read the code, never the display name.

## Fares
Unlike rail, etrain offers keep their full `variants[]` even in `compact`
(commuter fares are usually a single price, and there's NO read-only
etrain detail endpoint to recover them from — see below). Quote the fare
directly from `variants[]`.

Price basis: ONE SEAT (`meta.pricing.basis="per_seat"`). This search
takes no party size at all, so — unlike rail — nothing is totalled for
you: for N travellers multiply the fare yourself and present it as «от …
за N человек». Do not carry over the whole-party pricing of
`search_avia` / `search_bus`.

## Detail card
No separate read-only etrain detail endpoint.
`get_offer_details(product_type='etrain', details_ref=<offer>)` reformats
the selected search offer with a `ticket` block (eticket, by_passport,
plus `seat_assignment` and, when Tutu said anything,
`seat_assignment_note`) and surfaces `vehicle_type` in the summary. Etrain
offers carry NO `details_ref`, so you normally do not need this call at
all: `vehicle_meta.seat_assignment` is already on the search result.

## Checkout
`create_checkout_link` (transport=etrain) builds the tutu.ru commuter
schedule URL from `checkout_ref` (`departure_etrain_id` /
`arrival_etrain_id` -> st1/st2; station codes are fallback/debug fields).
It does NOT consume `offer_hash` — the schedule page is generic for the
route (no per-offer etrain deeplink exists). The field list is in the
tool's description.

## Cashback
Commuter trains earn none today, so `meta.cashback` is normally absent —
say nothing about cashback here. If the key IS there, it is the whole
page's Tutu loyalty rate: bonus points credited to the buyer's Tutu
account after payment, NOT money off `price`, never to be presented as a
discount. `applies_to` is `all_fares` / `most_fares` / `some_fares`,
with `rows_at_rate` of `rows_total` fare rows on the last two;
`exceptions[]` names the rows that differ and may be capped.

## Grounding
Schedule, stops and carrier facts come from this response — do not
substitute web lookups or general regional-rail knowledge when a field is
missing.
